flags.title: No structure sheet explicitly guarantees a one-entry maximum; S1 classifications are evidence-based
flags.detail: All 37 official DSE IV structure sheets were read. None explicitly says 'one entry only' or promises a freezeout. The site nevertheless marks 53 event rows 'Confirmed single-entry (standard S1)' because each row's own sheet was read and no rule grants a second entry under the published S1 test; this is not a venue guarantee. The other 41 rows are classified as multi-entry under the same standard. Obtain a written event-specific cap from the tournament desk before treating any event as a guaranteed freezeout. Per-row evidence and the full standard are on the Verification page. Re-read 2026-11-19 (session 0a0d8e6b, data/0a0d8e6b/sheet_reread.json): the 22 structure sheets behind the 53 rows were read line by line. Their start times, buy-ins, guarantees, starting chips, late-registration closes, house fees and prize pools match the stored rows on 53 of 53 rows. None of the 22 sheets contains a written one-entry, maximum-entry, re-entry, rebuy or add-on sentence. The label therefore means 'no re-entry, rebuy or add-on wording found on the sheet', not 'written single-entry rule'. User decision: keep the label with this definition, or relabel these rows as 'no re-entry wording found'.

flags.title: Venetian multi-flight events allow more than one entry
flags.detail: Events 01, 07, 19, 26, 47, 49, 56 and 59 have multiple starting flights, and each sheet carries the rule 'Any player who bags chips for Day 2 may not play a subsequent flight', which only restricts a player who has bagged. They are listed as multi-entry, not single-entry.

flags.title: Events #18 and #58 reference 'subsequent buy in's'
flags.detail: Structure sheet 8 (PokerAtlas Valuetown Bounty) states 'All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200', which shows more than one buy-in per player is possible.

flags.title: Every WPT / Wynn event whose terms were read permits re-entry
flags.detail: Re-checked 2026-11-19 against all 14 event sections in the official structures PDF: unlimited re-entry on the $600, $800, $1,100 PLO, $1,600, TORSE, HORSE, Mixed Triple Draw, Limit Omaha 8, Limit Omaha 8/Stud 8, $600 NLH Turbo and $1,600 PLO Mystery Bounty events; the $1,100 WPT Prime Championship allows one entry plus one re-entry per starting flight. The Wynn daily structures PDF likewise states a re-entry fee on its $200 events, and 'Re-entry is NOT allowed' only on the $240 Friday NLH Rebuy & Add-on, which sells extra chips by rebuy ($200 for 25,000 chips while at 15,000 or less) and one $100 add-on instead. No WPT/Wynn event of any kind meets standard S1.

flags.title: WPT schedule PDF date error: a block is labelled 'Dec. 18 Wednesday'
flags.detail: The block sits between Tuesday 15 December and Thursday 17 December and is headed 'Dec. 18 Wednesday'. 18 December 2026 is a Friday; the Wednesday of that week is 16 December. Those rows are dated 2026-12-16 here.

flags.title: Whole-page hashing marked 48 of 96 official sources 'changed' on the first nightly run
flags.detail: The monitor hashed every page as delivered. Casino pages carry per-request tokens and timestamps, so a 2-byte difference was recorded as a source change for half the ledger, and 'mark rows whose source changed' would have lit up rows whose values never moved. The monitor now compares extracted VALUES (scripts/monitor_b3be876c.py): the resort-fee sentence, the guarantee line, the registration-close line and the schedule row text. A row is marked only when one of those sentences changes; the raw page hash is kept as an informational column.

questions.how: Ask the Wynn poker room for the per-event structure sheets the schedule footnotes reference, and South Point for its rules sheets in text form; or read the full structures PDF past page 30 and the JPG rules sheets manually and record each Registration sentence with its URL and retrieval date. Treat every one of those rows as cap unknown until then.

suggestions.title: Put a one-line entry rule on every table row
suggestions.problem: A reader cannot tell at a glance whether an event is a freezeout, a re-entry or simply unknown.
options: Keep the three-way label (confirmed / multi-entry / unverified)
Add a plain-English sentence per row ('You may buy in again until 4:55 PM')
Add a colour-coded badge and drop the text
suggestions.effect: The second option costs one more column and removes most misreads. It does not change any data.

suggestions.title: Ask the poker rooms for a written single-entry statement
suggestions.problem: Silence on a structure sheet is not a one-entry promise, so nothing can be confirmed as a freezeout.
options: Email each room's tournament desk and publish the reply with a date
Photograph the printed structure sheet in the room on the day
Leave the rows unverified and plan around them
suggestions.effect: Only the first two can move an event from unverified to confirmed. Until then a freezeout plan is an assumption.

suggestions.title: Capture dated hotel quotes instead of a single number
suggestions.problem: Room rates move daily; a single figure goes stale and the true nightly cost with it.
options: Keep the dated rate log and paste a new quote each time you check
Add a screenshot field per log entry
Show only the resort fee and tax, which are stable
suggestions.effect: The log is the only option that keeps a like-for-like history. Screenshots make disputes resolvable.

suggestions.title: Time the walks yourself and record them
suggestions.problem: No official source publishes hotel-to-poker-room walking times, so the 30-minute filter is nearly empty.
options: Record the walking time you measure and store it with a date
Only accept on-property hotels until a walk is measured
Accept a third-party routing estimate and label it as an estimate
suggestions.effect: The first option makes the filter useful and stays honest. The third fills the table but is not an official value.

suggestions.title: Run the official-source check every morning, not once a day at random
suggestions.problem: Schedules, structures and fees change without notice.
options: GitHub Actions cron at 13:00 UTC (6 AM Las Vegas) every day
Twice daily (06:00 and 18:00 Las Vegas)
Weekly
suggestions.effect: A morning run matches the brief's 'pull the schedule each morning'. Twice daily catches intraday changes at double the Actions minutes.

suggestions.title: Publish one site instead of thirteen session dashboards
suggestions.problem: Earlier sessions each left a dashboard in its own folder; the same question has several different answers.
options: Keep this root site as the single answer and demote the rest to an archive index
Keep every dashboard and add a comparison page
Delete the older dashboards
suggestions.effect: The first option gives one answer per question and keeps earlier work reachable. Deleting loses source history.

suggestions.title: Price a plan that assumes one entry, and one that assumes re-entry
suggestions.problem: A multi-entry event can cost two, three or more buy-ins; a plan that assumes one entry understates the cost badly.
options: Show both totals side by side on the planner
Show only the single-entry total
Show a range with no assumptions stated
suggestions.effect: Side-by-side totals make the downside visible before you commit money.

suggestions.title: Reconfirm everything before any non-refundable payment
suggestions.problem: Every value here is a snapshot from an official page on 2026-11-17.
options: Re-run the source check and read the change log before booking
Call the room and the hotel to confirm
Book a refundable rate only
suggestions.effect: Refundable rates are the cheapest insurance; Caesars and Horseshoe advertise free 48-hour cancellation and Resorts World requires 48 hours' notice for a deposit refund.

suggestions.title: Capture dated stay quotes automatically in the morning job
suggestions.problem: The dated rate log currently holds hand-captured booking-engine snapshots; the trip planner stays Incomplete without a quote for the chosen dates and occupancy.
options: Extend the morning job to open each official booking link with fixed dates/occupancy and store whatever total the page shows (may fail: booking engines are JavaScript apps)
Keep captures manual but require a screenshot/link + timestamp before any booking decision
Subscribe to official rate-alert emails and log them as dated entries
suggestions.effect: A fresh dated quote per hotel per morning would make true nightly cost comparable like-for-like and let the planner complete honestly.

suggestions.title: Adopt a like-for-like comparison policy before any hotel ranking
suggestions.problem: Existing captures differ in stay window and occupancy (2 adults Dec 2-9 vs 1 adult Dec 13-20), so 'cheapest hotel' cannot be derived from them.
options: Rank nothing until two hotels share dates, occupancy and room class
Rank with an explicit comparability grade per row
Rank on nightly average and mark differing occupancy
suggestions.effect: Prevents a false ranking; the flagged page already refuses to name a cheapest hotel.

suggestions.title: Decide how walking minutes get verified
suggestions.problem: No official source publishes walking times between properties; the brief wants a 30-minute walking filter.
options: Keep minutes blank + provide one-click walking-direction links (current)
Record user-measured minutes via the routes page recorder (already available, browser-only)
Add a maps-distance service to the morning job and label its output as third-party estimates
suggestions.effect: The 30-minute filter can only be honest about measured or officially stated minutes.

suggestions.title: Decide the fate of the 13 archived session dashboards
suggestions.problem: Earlier session folders are published alongside the root site and disagree with it on some numbers.
options: Keep linked as read-only archives (current)
Move archives out of the published tree into git history only
Add a banner to each archive page pointing at the root site as the source of truth
suggestions.effect: Reduces reader confusion when an archived page shows an older verdict count.

suggestions.title: Publish one root-site generator (done here) and retire the second one
suggestions.problem: Two scheduled jobs each rebuilt the root site from different data with different verdict standards, so the published headline changed every night depending on which job committed last.
options: One canonical builder + an integration step, and a CI guard that fails when the committed site is not the canonical output (chosen, implemented)
Give each session its own subdirectory and never let a scheduled job write the root
Freeze the scheduled rebuilds entirely and rebuild only by hand
suggestions.effect: The site is reproducible: `python3 scripts/integrate_b3be876c.py && python3 scripts/build_ea99006a.py` regenerates every published page, and quality.yml proves the committed output matches.

suggestions.title: Keep value-level monitoring, drop hash-level alarmism
suggestions.problem: Hashing a whole casino page produces a 'change' on every request (tokens, timestamps), which buries real edits in noise; 48 of 96 ledger entries were 'changed' on the first run.
options: Compare extracted official sentences per value (implemented)
Keep page hashes but label them informational (kept)
Diff rendered text with a normalisation pass before hashing (future)
suggestions.effect: A row is marked 'source changed' only when the sentence behind its value changes.

suggestions.title: Filter the tables by whether an event is actually open to you
suggestions.problem: Single-entry rows can still be closed fields: the 2 and 8 December Seniors events pass S1 but are 50+, two LIPS satellites are female-only, and one event is a two-player tag team. Before this session they were ranked as ordinary picks and could become a day's primary event.
options: Keep the per-row 'entry restricted' label only (implemented)
Add a checkbox 'hide events I am not eligible to enter (Seniors 50+, female-only, tag team)'
Let the reader tick which field types they qualify for and filter on that
suggestions.effect: The label is implemented and the ranking plus the day schedule already exclude restricted rows. A reader-side toggle is the natural next step but needs a decision on what 'eligible' means (age and gender are the reader's own facts, not the site's to assume), so it is left as an option.

suggestions.title: Have the monitor record its first-read baseline explicitly
suggestions.problem: The whole-page ledger has no successful first read recorded, so its 'changed' marks are unproven and 94 schedule rows carry a page-level note that has nothing to do with their values (flag F57).
options: Leave it and keep the badge informational (the value-level monitor already compares sentences)
Seed the ledger on the next successful run as 'baseline', and only compare from the run after it
Drop the page-hash ledger and publish only value-level changes
suggestions.effect: Option 2 costs one scheduled run of extra latency and removes the misleading first-run badges; it does not change any published value.

suggestions.title: Close the remaining unverified rows: human-readable entry-terms capture
suggestions.problem: The rows that still carry an unverified label do so only because their official entry terms are not machine-readable in the build environment: the WPT structures PDF truncates at page 30 of extracted text, the per-event sheets its footnotes reference were not found published online, and South Point publishes its rules as JPG images.
options: A human reads the remaining WPT event terms and South Point rules sheets and pastes each entry sentence into data/ with its URL and retrieval date (fastest, no code)
Ask each room in writing for the entry cap per event (also resolves the F01 standard question)
Add OCR to the capture pipeline for the South Point JPG rules sheets
Leave the rows unverified and keep them out of every plan (current state, honest but incomplete)
suggestions.effect: Each closed row loses its unverified label and joins either the no-second-entry set or the multi-entry section, with the official sentence stored on the row.
